Translate a parsed formula into an INLA model

Source: R/formula.R
bm_inla_formula.Rd

Creates the INLA formula and the index columns it needs. Random effects, ordered() and strata() terms become f() terms with integer indices added to data.

Usage

bm_inla_formula(formula, data, response = "y", prior = bm_prior())

Arguments

formula

A formula, a character string, or a bm_formula object from bm_parse_formula().

data

Metadata data frame (samples in rows).

response

Name of the response variable in the INLA formula.

prior

A list of priors, as returned by bm_prior().

Value

An object of class bm_inla_model: a list with formula (the INLA formula, whose environment holds the hyperprior lists), data (the metadata with the added index columns), parsed (the bm_formula) and terms (a data frame describing each term).

Examples

meta <- data.frame(diagnosis = factor(c("CD", "UC", "nonIBD", "CD")),
                   age = c(20, 35, 50, 41),
                   subject = c("a", "a", "b", "b"))
m <- bm_inla_formula(~ diagnosis + age + (1 | subject), meta)
m$formula
#> y ~ 1 + diagnosis + age + f(.bm_re_subject, model = "iid", hyper = .bm_hyper$random)
#> <environment: 0x64c5a10da870>
